caseUseReview.evidence: No client or survey case is claimed; the packet's caseDecisions record that no approved case matched this reader question and none was forced. Attribution is limited to our own calculation, which is what the packet supports.

conditionsAndCounterexample.evidence: Counterexamples are on the page and in the packet: payoff at payment 48 gives $0 gap, 0% APR has nothing to allocate, small loans give $1.64, and a precomputed term over 61 months is outside the Rule of 78 under 1615(b) so the $227.82 case is labeled a formula illustration. The strongest primary-source counterexample, a precomputed consumer loan of 61 months or less, is stated as not addressed by the statute and left to contract and state law.

localExclusions.evidence: _experience.md section G excludes financial services from tested claims; page uses only calculated and reported labels (internal modeling attribution, CFPB and statute named by source) and no tested byline, method heading or tested schema. No medical or psychedelic content.

presentationReview.evidence: Interactive calculator plus static answer is the right format because loan amount, APR, term and payoff month change the gap; the key answer, tables and limits are readable without interaction. Calculator source shows labelled inputs, null-safe invalid input message, over-61-month notice, month table with caption and scroll wrapper and a text-labelled refund bar. Not verified in a browser at 390px; judged from source and the 391-check engine test.

renderedConsistency.evidence: Opener, tables, FAQ example, Is It Legal section and takeaway all use the same figures ($28.65, $1,269.31, $1,297.96, $88.13, $1.64, $0.00) and the same statutory scope; no figure on the page is absent from engine output. Writer's in-context fixes keep this consistent.

requestCoverage.evidence: Live-route render shows /rule-of-78-calculator/ with the data-tool island, whose figures come from src/lib/rule-of-78.ts; engine test script passes 391 checks; statute claims limited to 15 U.S.C. 1615 as verified against the text.

The rendered scope is additive: one new page and three link-only edits, no metadata, consolidation or redirect changes; exclusions accounting for the other queries is in the manifest and chart review (CR-5 dispositions) rather than on the page.

sourceAndAssumptions.evidence: Inputs are the sourced statute text and CFPB page plus explicit scenario inputs; assumptions (fixed rate, level payments, whole months, no fees, no state law, payoff right after a scheduled payment) are stated beside the results in the how-it-works section and the calculator footer. I re-derived all 8 scenarios and the 12-row schedule in an independent Python script (not the packet's model.mjs) and they match to the cent.

usefulness.evidence: The page answers the approved question (how the Rule of 78 splits interest and what early payoff costs): definition and $28.65 golden answer in the opener, formula and worked month 1 and month 48 figures, 12-row table, 7-scenario table, legality scope, calculator for the reader's own loan. It adds a decision-changing comparison against the actuarial method that the statute text alone does not give, so it is more than reworded sources.
